title: How Insurance Companies Make Money (The Float Explained)
alts: Why Insurance Companies Make Money Even When They Pay Claims
How Insurance Works: Buffett's $176 Billion Secret
line1: How do insurance companies make money? Twice: a small profit on premiums, and a giant one from investing your money first.
summary: Dave buys car insurance for his funny blue car and wonders where his $1,500 a year goes. We explain risk pooling with a simple village pot, premiums vs claims and the combined ratio, and the float: the money insurers invest before claims are paid. Berkshire Hathaway's float hit $176 billion in 2025 while it still made an underwriting profit. Plus why car insurance premiums rise, how deductibles work, why insurers can deny claims, and how Lloyd's of London began in a 1688 coffee house.
